Subject: Spectra is P0 - US-EAST1 AZ blacking out, requests immediate routing separation

Vivek / Marissa,

We're seeing a full AZ blackout affecting our US-EAST1 primary cluster. Errors started spiking at ~09:05 and token latencies jumped to 3-4s for our production traffic. Our SREs are seeing sustained 503s from the Redwood endpoints in the region and some KV cache misses. This is impacting the downstream lending flow (loan approvals) — we have customers in flight.

We've already opened a ticket on our side and collected traces (attached). Need to confirm Redwood's immediate routing plan and whether you can stage traffic to US-WEST2 + fallback model variants. Spectra is requesting:
- Immediate cross-region reroute for 30% of production traffic to reduce error blast radius
- A one-time token-cost credit if this was a Redwood routing failure
- A health summary for execs in 60 minutes

Please respond with the bridge URL and who will own the routing cut.

Thanks,
Alex Shaw
Head of Platform
Spectra Finance

Attachments: traffic_snapshot_20290814.json, spectra_error_samples.txt

Please stand by for the bridge invite; I'll add the Spectra SREs to read-only view of our dashboards.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 09:51:40 -0400
Subject: Re: Spectra is P0 - US-EAST1 AZ blacking out, requests immediate routing separation

Quick technical update from runtime:
- Root cause hypothesis: a regional autoscaler mis-applied a throttling policy during an infra config rollout at 09:01 which created a token-queue starvation on the US-EAST1 inference fleet. The nodes are healthy but admission layer is throttling new requests.
- Workaround planned: adjust admission limit and spin a temporary west pool with warmed KV caches. Siphon plan (Marissa) is good — we'll do 25% -> US-WEST2; latency expected to improve to ~300–450ms for routed traffic.
- Observability: enabling per-tenant logs for Spectra + adding an alert to suppress noisy paging for identical 503 bursts.

I'll push the config update now and post results in the bridge. If rollback of the autoscaler policy confirms improvement we'll follow with a postmortem and a compensating control to prevent future rollouts without a staged admission test.

— Rishi
Director, Inference Runtime

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Alex Shaw <alex.shaw@spectrafin.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Aug 2029 12:03:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Spectra is P0 - US-EAST1 AZ blacking out, requests immediate routing separation — executive note

Quick exec summary for Spectra and Leadership:
- Incident state: P0 impacting transaction approvals in US-EAST1 starting 09:05 EDT; immediate mitigation applied.
- Actions taken: controlled cross-region siphon (25% to US-WEST2, 10% to US-CENTRAL). Admission policy reverted; west pool warmed with KV caches. Error rate fell from 18% -> 1.2% on routed traffic; overall latency for routed requests down to 420ms median.
- Next steps: 1) complete forensic postmortem; 2) implement rollout guard to block throttling policy during autoscaler changes; 3) offer Spectra a one-time credit and a 3-month telemetry window for free.

Alex — I'll join your leadership call at 12:30 to walk through actions and proposed credit. Marissa will follow up with formal credit/contract language.

— Stephanie
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference
